Chapter 9. The Unfinished Story.
You know, not every story wraps up with a perfect ending. When Rie and Kido set out to uncover Daisuke’s true identity, they got as close to the truth as anyone probably could. But, some questions just stayed unanswered. The past, for them, became this patchwork—memories mixed with secrets—some of which, they realized, might never really come to light.
For Rie, coming to terms with the fact that she might never know everything was... well, it was both frustrating and oddly freeing. She’d spent months chasing answers, believing that if she just found the right piece, she’d finally get closure. But after a while, it hit her—closure doesn’t always show up in the form of facts or neat explanations. Sometimes, it’s something you build for yourself, bit by bit, in the way you choose to live moving forward.
As for Kido, he closed the case with a quiet sense of satisfaction. He knew he’d done everything he could. He’d helped Rie find a little understanding, even if the whole story would always be just out of reach. The experience left him a bit more humble, a bit more aware of how limited our knowledge can be.
Most of us want our stories to make sense, right? We want a clear beginning, a middle, and a satisfying end. But real life? It’s rarely that tidy. The threads of our past weave in and out of today, shaping tomorrow in ways we don’t always see coming—or control.
For Rie, the unfinished story of Daisuke became part of her own narrative—a reminder that life’s full of mysteries, and that the search for meaning isn’t something that just ends. She learned to live with the questions, to find a little comfort in the unknown, and to trust that, whatever came next, she had the strength to keep moving forward.
